sources.title: VAT Guide (1 November 2023 edition) — who must register (gross annual turnover above FJ$100,000, within 21 days), the zero-rated and exempt supplies, the right to deduct input tax (not on exempt supplies), tax invoices, accounting on the invoice basis unless the CEO approves the payment basis, taxable periods (monthly above FJ$300,000, three-monthly or yearly below) and their due dates, and the output and input adjustments

VAT Guide — rates and tax labels: 12.5 % (tax fraction 1/9) from 1 August 2025 on goods and services other than exempt and zero-rated ones, 15 % (3/23) from 1 August 2023, 0 % for the zero-rated supplies of Schedule 2, exempt supplies of Schedule 1; monthly, quarterly and annual filing; returns due on or before the last day of the month following the taxable period (Section 33 of the VAT Act)

Value Added Tax Return, form IRS217 (revised 26 November 2014): Section B boxes 1 to 6 (output tax), Section C boxes 7 to 12 (input tax), box 13 (amount to pay or refund due), and the panels for the output and input adjustments and the apportionment of input tax. The form prints the tax fraction of its day (9/109); the rate in force is the one of the rates source

Instructions for completing the VAT return (IRS217A, 28 July 2015): the thirteen boxes one by one — box 1 VAT-inclusive, box 3 = box 1 less box 2, box 4 = box 3 × tax fraction, box 7 from the input tax schedule, box 8 VAT invoiced by Customs on imports, box 13 may be negative (refund); an amount below FJ$5 is not remitted or refunded

Tax Talk — VAT Return Filing and the Return Lines: what the thirteen lines of the return relate to; exempt supplies (First Schedule of the VAT Act) stay out of line 1, zero-rated supplies (Second Schedule) are declared in lines 1 and 2 and keep the input tax credit

Use of IFRS Standards by jurisdiction — Fiji: the Fiji Institute of Accountants is the standard setter and has adopted IFRS Standards for large and publicly accountable entities and IFRS for SMEs for the others

IAS 1 Presentation of Financial Statements — the statement of financial position and the statement of profit or loss, expenses analysed by nature; no Fiji text prescribing a layout or a chart of accounts was found
Fiji Revenue and Customs Service — tax administration portal (forms, guides, the TPOS taxpayer portal on which VAT returns are filed and paid)

charts.name: Fiji reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in the texts read for Fiji: the Fiji Institute of Accountants sets the standards (IFRS Standards and IFRS for SMEs) and prescribes no chart. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-style statements below (IAS 1, expenses by nature), with the accounts a Fiji trading company keeps — VAT output and input tax, import VAT owed to FRCS at the border, PAYE withheld, FNPF (Fiji National Provident Fund) contributions and withholding taxes payable.

numbering.legal_reference: The tax invoice must state the words “tax invoice” (VAT Guide; instructions of the return); no text read states how invoices are numbered. `sequential` and the number format are conventions of this pack and not rules of the law.

tax_point.legal_reference: VAT Guide, chapter 10 — on the invoice basis VAT is accounted for at the earlier of the tax invoice, a payment received and the delivery; the payment basis needs the approval of the CEO of FRCS (public or local authorities, non-profit bodies, or taxable supplies under FJ$100,000 over 12 months). `invoice_date` is the pack's simplification of the invoice basis, and the payment basis is a gap recorded in the README.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No structured e-invoice standard, Peppol profile or clearance system of FRCS was found in the texts read; returns are filed and paid on the TPOS portal, which does not take invoices. `obligation` is `none` for want of a text, not on a finding that none exists.

not_taxed.legal_reference: The instructions of the return mention VAT reverse charge once, in box 7 (“including VAT Reverse Charge”), without saying which purchases it covers; the VAT Guide read has no chapter on services bought from abroad. The pack therefore carries no purchase tax for them. This is a finding about the texts read, not a finding that no reverse charge exists: it is a gap recorded in the README.
